title: Black Box Canberras: British Test and Trials Canberras 1951–1994
author: Dave Forster
note: Source heading misspells Forster as Foster; the reader's text and publisher establish Forster. Eligible history of experimental aircraft and equipment programs, not a flight or maintenance manual. Source researcher describes added explanatory context, so a high-confidence V3 veto is not established. T11 applies to the British program; T12 is zero because engineering trials are central. Explicit period endpoint 1994. Publisher gives 228 pages, while a dealer catalog gives 256; retain the publisher count with low page-count confidence and flag the disagreement. No supported veto found in inspected evidence.
notes: Source researcher reports extensive primary-source research; independent verification remains limited.
Links test aircraft, sensors, engines and research institutions.
Some reuse in test-platform strategy; much aircraft-specific detail.
Explains trial purposes and equipment relationships, with descriptive material alongside.

title: British Combat Aircraft in Latin America
author: Santiago Rivas
note: Eligible historical account of procurement and operations across several nations, not technical training or a routine report. Supplier choice and technology transfer supply some transferable value; do not apply V3 merely because detail is local. T11 is zero for the multinational scope. T12 applies to central military aviation and combat operations. The account begins around 1940 and extends to the contemporary retirement of these aircraft; 2019 is a low-confidence upper-bound endpoint, not a confirmed last event. No supported veto identified. Publisher gives 624 pages; RAeS catalog gives 621, a documented pagination discrepancy.
notes: Specialist historical account, but source checking and adverse reception not broadly inspected.
